passage:
During a science project, Nina found a woman scientist whose work had helped an important discovery but whose name was rarely mentioned.
She asked why some people disappear from history. Her teacher explained that records are shaped by power, culture, and who gets credit.
Nina made her report about both the discovery and the missing recognition. She did not try to make the scientist perfect. She tried to make her visible.
After the presentation, classmates asked about other forgotten people in textbooks.
History is not only about remembering. It is also about checking who was left out and why. Sometimes learning means adding names back to the story.
